sentences.text:
Applicant :- Rohit @ Karan
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. Of Home U.P. Civil Secrett. Lko
Counsel for Applicant :- Firoz Ahmad Khan

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Diwakar Singh,Manoj Kumar,Urvashi Vishwakarma
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Diwakar Singh, learned counsel for the informant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

2. In terms of the FIR, a missing person report was lodged subsequently however, in the statement under Section 161 & 164 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that both of them had gone together to Mumbai and there they stayed at a room.
It was also stated that both of them had married and stayed as husband and wife.

sentences.text: 3. The counsel for the informant filed an affidavit indicating that during examination at the time of trial, the victim has stated that she had gone along with the applicant to Mumbai and took a room and stayed there.
It was however stated that the marriage was performed by force, however, she admitted that she stayed with the applicant for 20-25 days.
Allegation of form of physical relation was also alleged.

4. In the light of the said, the counsel for the applicant argues that once the marriage is admitted,
offence under Section 376 IPC would not stand in view of exception 2 of Section 375 IPC.
The tentative age of the victim is around 17 years, which too not based upon any document which is prescribed in the Rules framed under the Juvenile Justice Act.
5. Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the bail prayer.

6. Considering the fact that the factum of marriage is admitted by the victim and there is no document to show that any proceedings were initiated declaring the said marriage null and void, the applicant is entitled to get the benefit of exception 2 of Section 375 of the IPC as the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 29.05.2023 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
7. Let the applicant Rohit @ Karan be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 190 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Raunahi, District Ayodhya,
on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
